channel.title: Houston Public Media - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Houston Public Media (houstonpublicmedia.org)

item.title: Cody Johnson sets concert attendance record to conclude 2026 Houston rodeo | Houston Public Media
item.description: A total of 2.6 million people attended the Houston rodeo this year held across three weeks at NRG Park.

item.title: State of the energy industry (March 24, 2026) | Houston Public Media
item.description: On Tuesday's show: We learn about events, speakers, and protests happening during the annual CERAWeek energy conference this week in Houston and we dig into the state of the energy industry amid ever-rising oil prices.

item.title: Fire out and shelter-in-place order is lifted after oil refinery explosion in Port Arthur | Houston Public Media
item.description: No one was injured in Monday's explosion at a Valero refinery near the Texas coast, Port Arthur Mayor Charlotte M. Moses said.

item.title: Texas Education Agency orders public schools to remove mentions of César Chávez from lessons | Houston Public Media
item.description: Schools were also directed to cancel or change celebrations of the late civil rights leader amid allegations of sexual abuse.

item.title: Hourslong security lines at Bush Airport leave Houston travelers missing flights, rebooking while they wait | Houston Public Media
item.description: The Trump administration sent ICE agents to airports in Houston and across the U.S. on Monday to assist TSA workers, many of whom are calling out sick amid a partial government shutdown that began in mid-February.

item.title: The week in politics (March 25, 2026) | Houston Public Media
item.description: On Wednesday's show: We discuss the latest developments in politics in our weekly roundup. And we consider whether Texas is too big.

item.title: Hello Houston (March 24, 2026) | Houston Public Media
item.description: Today: We discuss the expansion of Ben Taub Hospital, talk with Broadway star Nicholas Rodriguez about his musical tribute to Stephen Sondheim, explore the growing concerns over social security, and more.

item.title: Hello Houston – The Commuter Cut (March 24, 2026) | Houston Public Media
item.description: For our busy Houston commuters, we have – The Commuter Cut – a special 40-minute version of our show to listen to during your journey home.

item.title: ‘Difficult to assess’: Oil CEOs, energy experts weigh impacts of Iran war during CERAWeek | Houston Public Media
item.description: While U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright described the war as "temporary," energy CEOs, many of them headquartered in Houston, offered a more uncertain outlook.

item.title: NASA could launch Artemis II to the moon next week. Here’s what to know | Houston Public Media
item.description: From launch dates to mission plans, Houston Public Media explains everything you need to know about the historic Artemis II mission.

item.title: Prepare to pay up for last-minute UH v. Illinois Sweet 16 tickets | Houston Public Media
item.description: As of Wednesday morning, the cheapest seats on offer in the approximately 19,000-seat Toyota Center were running for $408 on AXS. The most expensive resale ticket, at half court, was going for more than $8,000.

item.title: Houston Mayor Whitmire accused Controller Hollins of ‘pay-to-play.’ What did a probe find? | Houston Public Media
item.description: The accusation was a flashpoint in the tense relationship between the city’s top executive and its chief financial official.

item.title: Abbott legal brief criticizes Paxton’s rushed lawsuit against Harris County’s immigrant legal fund | Houston Public Media
item.description: “Perhaps the Attorney General only recently learned of this program; perhaps the office’s attention was focused elsewhere,” lawyers for Abbott wrote, noting the fund has existed for five years.

item.title: How Texas could soon have more AI data centers than anywhere else in the world | Houston Public Media
item.description: Pacifico Energy and other energy companies are rushing to build private power plants across the Lone Star State.

item.title: Texas will require proof of legal immigration status to get professional licenses | Houston Public Media
item.description: Officials approved the change after hearing from speakers who argued it would hamper the state’s economy and push immigrants to work without licenses in the black market.
